items.title: How many earlier expectations must grow as the checker gains rules?
items.description: Grounded in L3's password checker: after the empty-input cycle, each new rule (length, uppercase, number) forces every earlier test whose input fails it to list one more message. The uppercase rule updated 1 earlier expectation ("short"), the number rule updated 2 ("short" and "longenough"), 3 edits in total at the 3 rules the unit builds. Drag the number of rules and watch the total climb faster than the rule count. These edits are deliberate spec changes made in the open, so the cost is real but honest; it is why a refactor toward a rule list is worth doing before the list gets long. The model assumes each earlier test's input satisfies only the rules built before it, as in the unit.

params.name: rules
params.label: Rules in the finished checker (after the empty-input check)

items.compute: const n = params.rules; return { totalEdits: n * (n - 1) / 2, editsForLastRule: n - 1 };
